subject: Renewal pricing & bridge credit — Cobalt Systems
messages:
From: Ethan Liu <ethan.liu@cobalt-systems.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@cobalt-systems.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning for Q3 — capacity bump & pricing

Hi Ava,

Hope you're well. Our contract term with Redwood ends June 30 and we've seen sustained growth in inference usage — spike started in March and Q1 finished ~2.5x our baseline. We're planning a capacity increase to support a new recommendation feature and would like to align on renewal pricing before procurement starts the RFP process.

Questions:
- Can you provide options for (a) a 12-month renewal with a mid-term capacity bump and (b) a 24-month committed plan with upfront credits?
- Are there standard bridge-credit mechanics you offer for overages during a ramp?
- Would Redwood consider a short price-hold while we finalize SKU consolidation internally?

I can pull recent usage numbers if helpful. Procurement's looped on this thread — they'd like ballpark economics and any request we need to expect from legal.

Thanks,
Ethan Liu
Head of ML Platform
Cobalt Systems

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Liu <ethan.liu@cobalt-systems.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning for Q3 — capacity bump & pricing

On Tue, Apr 20, 2027 at 09:15 AM Ethan Liu <ethan.liu@cobalt-systems.com> wrote:
> Hope you're well. Our contract term with Redwood ends June 30 and we've seen sustained growth...

Thanks for the heads up, Ethan — congrats on the product momentum. I'd propose three clean options so procurement and legal can pick a path:

Option A — 12-month term (fast lane)
- Commit increase to 120M tokens/mo (from current 50M)
- 10% baseline discount across generation tokens
- One-time bridge credit equal to 15% of overage costs for the first billing quarter to smooth ramp
- Price-hold for 90 days from signature
- Minimal legal changes; can do via amendment

Option B — 24-month term (savings-first)
- Commit increase to 120M tokens/mo
- 18% baseline discount + SKU consolidation credit (8% effective additional saving on consolidated SKUs)
- Upfront prepayment credit applied over first 6 months to reduce bill volatility
- Price-hold for 180 days

Option C — 18-month hybrid (middle ground)
- Commit to 100M tokens/mo with step-up to 140M after month 6
- 14% discount, bridge credit 20% of overage for month 1 only, 10% for month 2
- Short price-hold (120 days)

Attached is a template usage CSV and a quick P&L model (Cobalt-usage-report-q1.csv) that we use to map commits to unit economics. Can you confirm anticipated monthly peaks and whether the SKU consolidation you're doing will remove any high-cost endpoints?

I'll loop Ben (account exec) and Aditya (solutions) to help size infra and confirm feasibility on our end. If procurement wants a single recommended path, our calibration is that Option B gives the best unit economics for you given a sustained 2.5x increase.

Next steps:
- You share a short-term usage run-rate (next 6 months) + legal must-haves
- We send a redline-ready amendment and a DocuSign offer for signature

Best,
Ava Chen
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124

From: Procurement <procurement@cobalt-systems.com>

Cc: Maya Singh <maya@skybridgepartners.com>, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning for Q3 — capacity bump & pricing

Ava,

Thanks for the options. We've reviewed with finance; procurement prefers a single-line item that preserves flexibility for the first 6 months while we validate performance. A couple of notes and redlines:

- Request a 6-month price-hold from signature (noted in Option B) before any rate changes apply.
- We'd like bridge-credit mechanics spelled out: percentage of overage credited as account-level credit applied to next invoice.
- Please itemize SKUs as separate line items — we need a clear mapping for our internal chargeback.
- Legal will want a clause limiting liability on model output; expect a short review.

I've attached a PO draft (Cobalt_PO_0428.pdf) with our internal reference. Procurement is OK with Option B economics if the legal and price-hold terms are satisfied.

Procurement (on behalf of Cobalt Systems)
procurement@cobalt-systems.com

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Procurement <procurement@cobalt-systems.com>, Ethan Liu <ethan.liu@cobalt-systems.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: 18-month consolidated offer + bridge credit (next steps)

Ethan / Procurement team — thanks for the back-and-forth and the PO. Per procurement's preference to preserve flexibility, we've worked up a final consolidated offer that balances unit economics with the operational softness you need during ramp. Summary below (we can produce a 1-page amendment):

Final proposal (we recommend the hybrid):
- Term: 18 months (effective on signature)
- Commit profile: 100M tokens/mo for months 1–6; auto-step to 140M tokens/mo from month 7 onward
- Commit pricing: 14% discount vs public list across generation tokens
- SKU consolidation credit: 8% effective discount applied to consolidated endpoints for duration of term
- Bridge credit: One-time credit equal to 20% of overage charges during the first billing month post-signature (credit applied to next invoice)
- Price-hold: 180 days (we will not increase unit rates during this period)
- Legal: Limited additional redline items accepted; Redwood standard model-output clause with mutual indemnity language is acceptable pending a 5-business-day legal review

Attachments: COB-Docusign-Offer-0509.pdf (final amendment + DocuSign envelope), and we preserved your PO reference in the DocuSign packet.

If this aligns, please reply "Approve and sign" and we'll trigger DocuSign and copy legal for the short review. Once signed, our operations team will kick off quota changes and Ben will coordinate the initial migration windows for SKU consolidation. Monica (CS lead) is on copy to scope the onboarding runbook.

Thanks — looking forward to getting you scaled.

Ava Chen
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124
